title: Finite lifting criterion for naturally marked quasicategories
statement: Use the small simplicial sets, horns, quasicategories and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and the marked simplicial sets, right lifting properties, maps (i), (ii), (iii) and finite marked map $A^\flat\to A$ of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. Let $Z$ be any small marked simplicial set, and let $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{fin}}$ consist of all the maps (i), (ii), (iii), together with $A^\flat\to A$; thus it does not include the maps (iv) for arbitrary Kan complexes. The map $Z\to(\Delta^0)^\sharp$ has the right lifting property against $\mathcal J_{\mathrm{fin}}$ if and only if the underlying simplicial set $Q$ is a quasicategory and the marked edges of $Z$ are exactly the equivalences of $Q$, that is, $Z=Q^\natural$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7, proof (1), printed pp. 158-159, specialized to S=Delta^0; Proposition 3.1.1.6, proof, printed pp. 149-150, for the horn-lifting part. The finite A detector replaces the arbitrary Kan-complex generators (iv). Read online 2026-10-17; no Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Assume the stated right lifting property. Every underlying inner horn map to $Q$ is a marked map from its minimally marked horn, so lifting against (i) makes $Q$ a quasicategory by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $f$ be a marked edge. Every final outer horn with final edge $f$ is a marked map from the domain of (ii), and its lift supplies an underlying filler. This holds for every $n\geq2$. The converse final-outer-horn criterion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling] therefore makes $f$ an equivalence. Thus the marking contains no non-equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, proof of (A) and the first implication in (B), specialized to a point; Proposition 1.2.4.3 and its opposite.

proof.text: Now let $f:x\to y$ be any equivalence of $Q$, without assuming it marked. By the inverse-triangle definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], choose $g:y\to x$ and a triangle $\tau$ on vertices $(y,x,y)$ with edges $g,f,\mathrm{id}_y$. Form a horn $\Lambda_3^3\to Q$ on vertices $(x,y,x,y)$ by prescribing its faces $d_0=\tau$, $d_1=s_0f$, and $d_2=s_1f$. The faces $d_0,d_1$ meet on $[2,3]$, where both prescriptions give $f$; $d_0,d_2$ meet on $[1,3]$, where both give $\mathrm{id}_y$; and $d_1,d_2$ meet on $[0,3]$, where both give $f$. Thus the prescriptions agree on every intersection. Its final edge $[2,3]=f$ is an equivalence. The forward final-outer-horn assertion of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling], with $n=3$, supplies a filler $\sigma$. Hence $d_1\sigma=s_0f$ and $d_2\sigma=s_1f$. By the defining corepresenting property of the finite detector in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus], the pair $(\sigma,f)$ gives an underlying map $u:A\to Q$. The edge $[0,1]$ maps to $f$, as is seen on the face $d_2\sigma=s_1f$. This construction uses an unmarked horn filler and does not assume the conclusion that $f$ is marked.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7(1), finite detector and extension of an equivalence to A; explicit final-outer-3-horn argument using Proposition 1.2.4.3 instead of a weak-equivalence extension argument.

proof.text: The underlying map $u$ of Step 2 defines a marked map $A^\flat\to Z$, because its only marked edges are degeneracies. Put it in the lifting square against $A^\flat\to A$, with the unique bottom map to $(\Delta^0)^\sharp$. A diagonal $A\to Z$ has the same underlying map $u$, since the left map is the identity on underlying simplicial sets. The added marked edge $[0,1]$ of $A$ must therefore map to a marked edge of $Z$. Its image is $f$. Every equivalence is consequently marked; together with Step 1 this proves $Z=Q^\natural$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.3.7(1), use of the finite detector inclusion to force the equivalence marking, specialized to a point.

proof.text:
Conversely suppose $Z=Q^
atural$. The lifting characterization in [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus] gives lifting against every marked-anodyne map, in particular (i), (ii), and (iii). For completeness the extra detector map requires no membership in that class: for any underlying $u:A	o Q$, write its defining pair as $(\sigma,e)$. The equations $d_1\sigma=s_0e$ and $d_2\sigma=s_1e$ give $[0,1]=[2,3]=[0,3]=e$ and make $[0,2]$ and $[1,3]$ identity edges. Write $e:x	o y$; the vertices of $\sigma$ are then $(x,y,x,y)$. With $g=[1,2]:y	o x$, the remaining faces $d_3\sigma$ and $d_0\sigma$ witness $g\circ e=\mathrm{id}_x$ and $e\circ g=\mathrm{id}_y$, respectively. Thus the image of the one additional marked edge $[0,1]$ is an equivalence, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Every marked map $A^ lat	o Q^
atural$ therefore extends, with unchanged underlying map, to $A	o Q^
atural$. This supplies the last required lift. All horns and the detector are finite, and all constructions take place inside the fixed input universe; the argument also applies to the empty quasicategory.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q86-f19333eea (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its four proof steps and the full statements of the four nodes it cites (def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones, lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus, lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling, def-weil-size-convention). The delivery adds no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. Step 1: lifting against (i) gives inner fillers. For n>=2 the edge [n-1,n] lies in face d0 of the final horn, so any final horn ending in a marked f is a valid lifting problem for (ii). The converse clause of the outer-horn node then makes f an equivalence. Step 2: I checked the 3-horn on vertices (x,y,x,y) by hand. The faces are d0 = tau = (g,f,id_y), d1 = s0 f and d2 = s1 f. They agree on the shared edges [2,3]=f, [1,3]=id_y and [0,3]=f, and the final edge is f. The filler sigma satisfies the defining relations of the calculus node's detector A, and [0,1] maps to f. Step 3 is correctly marked elementary: A-flat to A is the identity on underlying simplicial sets, so any diagonal keeps the map u and forces f to be marked. Step 4: (i)-(iii) follow from the calculus node's stated characterization of the full class. The relations of A force vertices 0=2, 1=3, the edges [0,1]=[2,3]=[0,3]=e and degenerate [0,2],[1,3], and d3, d0 are the two inverse triangles. Small cases behave correctly: the empty set (lifting vacuous), the n=1 case of (ii), degenerate f, N(0->1) with a non-equivalence marked (the (1,0,1) final horn has no filler), and a groupoid nerve with an unmarked isomorphism (fails the detector lift). No duplicate exists: the DAG nodes that mention the detector and the HTT places state the model structure, the relative versions or the full-class criterion, and those need (iv). No cycle: the closures of the four cited nodes do not contain the item. I accept the declared tool use of lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling; the same node is already an accepted tool use in six nodes of this unit. HTT is not archived locally, so the WANTED line and proof_origin by agent are correct; I checked the proof against the DAG's own definition of A instead.
